I am 65 years old, and I have farmed these 15 mu in Anzhai Township, Quzhou County, for 42 years. My wife and I are the only ones left in the household, so I cannot take risks or spread myself too thin. I finished high school, which in my day was rare in the village, so I can read the county extension office's bulletins and understand fertilizer labels. I do not follow every new fad, but I pay attention to what works on my soil.

This year, I will plant cotton on all 15 mu. It is the crop I know best, and the local cotton market in Quzhou is reliable. I will buy hybrid cotton seeds — I have used guoxinmian varieties before and they perform well here. I will plough the field in early April before sowing. Some neighbors use rotary tillage because it is faster, but after four decades I know that deep ploughing helps cotton roots grow deep, and with my well, deep roots mean better drought resistance.

For fertilizer, I will apply 16 kg of nitrogen per mu. I split it — base dressing at sowing and top-dressing at flowering. Too much nitrogen makes the plants grow too tall and leafy, which brings pests and reduces boll set. I will add 7 kg of phosphorus and 10 kg of potassium per mu. Cotton needs plenty of potassium when the bolls are forming; I learned that lesson years ago from the extension pamphlets.

My well gives me water, but pumping costs electricity. I will irrigate three times: once at sowing if the spring is dry, once at early flowering in July, and once at peak boll filling in August. Three well-timed irrigations are enough on this soil. I have tried four, and it does not pay for the extra pump hours.

For pesticides, the hybrid seeds help with bollworm, but I still need to spray for aphids, spider mites, and whiteflies. I walk the fields every morning during the growing season. I will spray four times this year, only when I see the pests reaching threshold. That saves money and keeps the plants healthy.

If the weather cooperates and I manage the water right, I expect about 520 kg of seed cotton per mu this year. Last year I got 500 kg/mu. With careful timing, 520 kg is realistic.
